audit_findings.title: Growth may be valued without the land and inventory reinvestment required to produce it
audit_findings.magnitude: $521.2 million FY2025 inventory cash use and $900.4 million 9M FY2026 inventory cash use; a computed $83.8 million recurring OE reduction would erase the $8.72 price-to-buy-below cushion
audit_findings.mechanism: Normalized land, inventory and joint-venture reinvestment reduces distributable OE and must increase with scenario growth.
audit_findings.evidence: This activity was offset, in part, by an increase of $521.2 million in inventory, a decrease of $66.7 million in net customer deposits; a $24.8 million increase in receivables, prepaid expenses and other assets, $21.1 million in current income taxes, net, and $7.6 million in mortgage loan originations, net of sales.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is not demonstrated because the line-by-line OE calculation was not supplied. It is nevertheless materially capable: only a small fraction of the filed inventory cash uses would need to represent omitted recurring reinvestment to reverse the valuation conclusion. The reported movements cannot be deducted mechanically because they include timing, growth and acquisition effects.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to cash flow, separate maintenance from growth inventory and joint-venture funding, and rerun every scenario with explicit reinvestment tied to deliveries, community growth and RONTA.

audit_findings.title: Joint-venture sale gains and stake value may be counted twice
audit_findings.magnitude: $45.1 million FY2025 recognized sale gain and $907.082 million July 2026 stakes bridge; capitalizing $45.1 million dollar-for-dollar at the base DCF factor would add a computed $633.7 million, or about $4.70 per share to buy-below
audit_findings.mechanism: Stake-related income or disposition gains retained in OE are capitalized while the underlying investments are also added through stakes_net.
audit_findings.evidence: From our investments in these joint ventures we received cash and recognized our share of the gains of $45.1 million in fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the $45.1 million gain entered FY2025 earnings, but the record does not show whether it or other stake-related income was removed from the $1.305 billion OE anchor. The known gain alone, even conservatively treated without a tax reduction, would not erase the $8.72 buy-below cushion; the unreconciled income attributable to all $907.082 million of stakes is unquantified, so total materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile OE to net income and remove after-tax equity-method income, disposition gains and non-arm's-length fees attributable to separately valued stakes; then rerun the DCF without changing the stake valuation.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter conflicts with the completed multifamily exit
audit_findings.magnitude: $420.969 million held-for-sale assets and $172.186 million related liabilities at October 2025; approximately $330.0 million net cash proceeds in FY2026; reported FY2026 sale-related amounts include $18.8 million land gain, $72.1 million ownership-interest gains, $56.7 million JV asset-sale gains, $97.4 million impairments and $10.0 million deferred fees
audit_findings.mechanism: The pre-disposition OE anchor may include sold-business income, losses, gains and fees while the post-disposition bridge contains proceeds and only retained investments and obligations.
audit_findings.evidence: In December 2025, we completed a significant portion of the sale to Kennedy Wilson, including our operating platform, with the remaining portion expected to occur in the first half of our fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter inconsistency is demonstrated: FY2025 earnings and a null perimeter are combined with a July 2026 balance sheet after the sale was substantially completed. Direction is mixed because removing sale gains and lost fees lowers OE, while removing disposed-business losses raises it. The filed record does not isolate the sold operations' normalized after-tax OE, so the net valuation effect and materiality cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Create a sold-versus-retained perimeter through July 2026, reconcile proceeds into cash, remove all disposed-business recurring results and transaction items from OE, retain only continuing interests and obligations, and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may include customer-funded or operational cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,057.889 million maximum bridge exposure; removing the entire amount would reduce base value by about $11.20 per share and buy-below by about $7.84 to $142.61
audit_findings.mechanism: Only excess cash belongs in the equity bridge; operating liquidity or cash associated with deposits and obligations should remain with the operating business.
audit_findings.evidence: Our contract liabilities, consisting of deposits received from customers for sold but undelivered homes, totaled $ 418.9 million, $ 488.7 million, and $ 540.7 million at October 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The surplus-cash classification is unresolved, and July 2026 customer deposits were $458.123 million. However, even the deliberately conservative removal of the entire cash/STI add-back leaves the computed $142.61 buy-below above the $141.73 market price by about $0.88. This finding alone therefore cannot change the stated valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash to restricted balances, customer deposits, minimum operating liquidity, land obligations and sale proceeds, and replace the bridge amount with demonstrably excess cash for accuracy.

audit_findings.title: Joint-venture guarantees are claims ahead of common equity not captured by ordinary debt
audit_findings.magnitude: $388.9 million July 2026 maximum repayment and carry-cost exposure plus $122.5 million retained exposure on sold ventures, or $511.4 million gross; filed guarantee fair value was $12.4 million; completion and indemnity exposure is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A guarantee call or an omitted current guarantee liability reduces stake value or creates an equity claim outside ordinary consolidated debt.
audit_findings.evidence: At October 31, 2025, the unconsolidated entities had borrowed an aggregate of $1.46 billion, of which we estimate $413.5 million to be our maximum exposure related to repayment and carry cost guarantees.
audit_findings.explanation: No significant guarantee payments had occurred, collateral was expected to cover much of the obligations, and Kennedy Wilson reimbursement agreements cover the $122.5 million sold-venture exposure. Even deducting the entire $511.4 million gross amount would lower buy-below by about $3.79 to $146.66, still above the market price. Unquantified completion guarantees remain a forward-looking contingent risk rather than a demonstrated present loss.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the $12.4 million recorded guarantee fair value is reflected in stakes_net, obtain venture-level collateral and partner-reimbursement schedules, stress-test gross guarantee calls, and monitor refinancing or release of the Kennedy Wilson guarantees.

audit_findings.title: The assertion that interest remains inside OE is incomplete because most interest is capitalized
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 interest incurred exceeded home and land interest expensed by a computed $12.403 million; the corresponding 9M FY2026 gap was $13.810 million; treating the larger gap as recurring OE would reduce buy-below by about $1.44
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash interest is paid when incurred but enters accounting earnings later through inventory cost, creating a timing difference in OE if current cash interest and inventory investment are both omitted.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023, the Company’s qualified inventory exceeded its indebtedness and substantially all interest incurred, excluding interest related to our mortgage company subsidiary’s operations, was capitalized to inventory.
audit_findings.explanation: Capitalization and the timing lag are demonstrated, but omission from OE is not because the detailed OE reconciliation is absent. The filed timing gaps are well below the computed $83.8 million recurring OE reduction needed to erase the valuation cushion. Even treating the larger nine-month gap as a permanent, dollar-for-dollar OE overstatement would not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile interest incurred, interest released through home and land cost of revenues, joint-venture capitalization and ending capitalized interest for every anchor year; ensure each cash interest dollar is charged exactly once.
